subject.title: RFC: Skill routing metadata and evaluation hints for Harness-style OpenClaw setups

question: Should ClawHub adopt a narrow, explicitly advisory v1 routing-and-verification metadata contract, and which fields may be publisher-supplied without being treated as policy or trust evidence?
rationale: The repository already supports additive metadata and public discovery, but choosing field semantics, trust treatment, and API exposure determines a durable registry contract and cannot be safely inferred from this RFC alone.

options.title: Adopt a narrow advisory v1
options.body: Start with bounded routing intents and human-readable verification hints exposed as raw metadata, while explicitly excluding enforcement, ranking guarantees, and publisher-declared risk from trust decisions.

options.title: Defer until consumer evidence exists
options.body: Keep the current metadata and revisit after a Harness or other client can demonstrate the exact retrieval and evaluation contract it needs.

options.title: Expand registry policy signals
options.body: Treat risk and preflight fields as a broader trust product, requiring a separate security design, validation model, and moderation ownership.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow advisory v1
recommendation.body: Start with bounded routing intents and human-readable verification hints exposed as raw metadata, while explicitly excluding enforcement, ranking guarantees, and publisher-declared risk from trust decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged structured-manifest work is the closest concrete implementation precedent, though final contract ownership is not established by the available history.
